subject: Retention and backup purge: subprocessor mapping & exception ask
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Retention and backup purge: subprocessor mapping & exception ask

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the DPA review earlier this week. Attached is the Appendix B excerpt we propose (Wellbridge_DPA_AppendixB.pdf) plus the latest subprocessor matrix (subprocessor_matrix_v3.xlsx) that maps retention windows across our storage tiers, backups, and audit logs.

A few items we want to clarify and ask for your signoff on:

- Backup purge cadence: Our standard production backup retention for tokens/logs is 90 days in hot backups, then a rolling 180-day cold snapshot retention before final deletion. For Wellbridge we can compress that to 60/120 for application data but we need an exception to retain ephemeral forensic logs for 180 days to support incident investigations.
- Log retention exception: We are requesting a 180-day forensic log retention carveout (vs. default 90 days) for two reasons: regulatory support for investigations, and to match the retention on your audit tooling.
- Subprocessor disclosure: The attached matrix lists third parties that have backup access for restoration (S3 transfer agents, Vault key escrow, on-call forensic partner). Please confirm if any of these require a named subprocessor approval process from your side or if blanket disclosures suffice.

Can you review and confirm if Wellbridge is ok with the 180-day forensic log exception and the modified 60/120 backup cadence for application data? If you prefer, we can set up a 30-minute call with procurement to finalize the Annex language.

Thanks —
Avery

--

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retention and backup purge: subprocessor mapping & exception ask

Hi Avery —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick answers up front:

- We generally prefer shorter backup windows for PII and PHI; the 60/120 split looks reasonable as a starting point, but we need the forensic logs carveout to be justified and scoped narrowly.
- Forensic logs: we can consider 180 days for server-side audit logs (authentication events, admin actions) but not for user content.
- Subprocessors: we require named approval for any subprocessor that can access decrypted backups (i.e., key custodians or on-call restore vendors). The others can be covered by a disclosure, not explicit approval.

Could you add an explicit section in Appendix B showing which subprocessors have decryption/key access? Liam from procurement is cc'd — he will want a short SLA table and DocuSign-ready language for the exception.

Would you and Kimberly be available for a 30-minute call Thursday 11/05 at 10:00am PT to walk through the Annex and the subprocessor/key map?

Best,
Sofia

--
Sofia Martens
Head of Security Compliance
Wellbridge Health

Avery / team —

Thanks — I made a few suggested changes to Appendix B and the subprocessor matrix to specifically call out decrypt-capable subprocessors and the operational controls we will apply. See attached redlines_DPA_appendixB.pdf. Key points we should propose on the call:

1) Scoped forensic logs: define categories (auth/admin vs. user content). We should limit content retention unless explicitly required by a legal hold.
2) Decrypt-capable subprocessors: name them in Appendix B and add a one-line attestation for each (SOC 2 Type II, yearly pen test, contractual obligation to notify on data access).
3) SLA & purge workflow: commit to a documented purge runbook with a 48-hour notification to Wellbridge before any cross-region snapshot deletion, and a 10-business-day remediation window for contested deletions.

If Sofia is comfortable, I can join the Thursday 10:00am PT call and we can present the draft language. Also recommend we add a DocuSign envelope for the Appendix so procurement can sign the exception without redlining the main DPA.

-Kim

Subject: Final: Wellbridge retention carveouts & DocuSign request

Sofia / Liam —

Thanks for the productive call last week. Summary of what we agreed and next steps: 

- Backup cadence: Wellbridge accepted the 60-day hot / 120-day cold snapshot cadence for application data.
- Forensic logs exception: Agreed scope — 180 days for server-side auth/admin audit logs only; no user content. This is captured in Appendix B section 2.1.
- Decrypt-capable subprocessors: We will list the two vendors with key escrow access in Appendix B and provide SOC 2 attestations (on file).
- Purge workflow: Redwood will provide a purge runbook and will give 48-hour notice before cross-region snapshot deletions; contested deletions will trigger a 10-business-day remediation window.

Next actions:
- Kimberly to upload final redline + clean Appendix and DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.net/Wellbridge/Envelope/ABC123
- Wellbridge to sign the Appendix (envelope sent by Kimberly) or propose further edits by EOD 11/17.
- Audit team (audit@rsync-audit.com) will receive the SOC reports; Avery will share the secure drive link.

If there are no further edits, we'll treat Appendix B as an Annex executed by DocuSign and attach to the master DPA.

Thanks again —
Avery
